findings.description: jwt.decode only base64-decodes the token and does not verify the signature, even though SECRET is loaded and unused. Any caller can forge claims.
findings.scenario: Send 'Authorization: Bearer <unsigned token with sub=<admin user id>>'. The token is accepted and req.user is set to that user. A malformed token makes decode return null, so claims.sub throws a TypeError, which is passed to next(err) as a 500.
findings.fix: const claims = jwt.verify(token, SECRET, { algorithms: ['HS256'] }); and return 401 on verification failure.

findings.description: `req.user.role = 'admin'` assigns instead of comparing. The condition is always truthy, so every authenticated user passes and is also mutated to admin in memory (and persisted if the user object is saved later).
findings.scenario: A regular user with role 'user' calls an admin route. requireAdmin sets role to 'admin' and calls next().

findings.description: revokeSessions uses req.params.id taken straight from the URL and never checks it against req.user or admin rights. It is not shown to be guarded by requireAdmin, and requireAdmin is itself broken.
findings.scenario: Any authenticated user calls the revoke endpoint with another user's id and logs that user out of all their sessions.
findings.fix: Require req.user.id === req.params.id or a correct admin check before listing and deleting sessions.

findings.description: forEach with an async callback does not wait for the deletes. The response is sent before any deletion completes, and a rejected db.sessions.delete becomes an unhandled rejection that crashes or is lost while the client is told they were revoked.
findings.scenario: If db.sessions.delete fails or is slow, res.json({revoked: total}) still reports success while sessions remain valid. On Node 15+ the unhandled rejection can terminate the process.
findings.fix: await Promise.all(sessions.map(s => db.sessions.delete(s.id))); inside try/catch, and report the actual count.

findings.description: Sessions are listed with a limit (default 50, caller-controlled, unbounded), so revocation only covers that many sessions. The response claims 'revoked' equals the number listed.
findings.scenario: A user with 200 sessions: the call revokes only 50 and returns revoked: 50. The remaining 150 stay valid. A negative or huge limit is also accepted.
findings.fix: Delete all sessions for the user (e.g. a deleteAllByUser call) or loop until none remain; do not take the limit from the client for a security operation.

findings.description: SECRET is exported from the module, widening access to the signing key to any importer.
findings.scenario: Any module that requires this file can read or log the JWT signing secret.
findings.fix: Remove SECRET from module.exports and expose only signing/verifying helpers.
